title: Short Stuff: Roly Poly...Bugs?
summary: Short Stuff episode on roly polies (pill bugs, potato bugs, woodlice), land-dwelling crustaceans from the Mediterranean spread worldwide via the plant trade. The hosts cover their common names by region, that they are crustaceans rather than insects, their ability to roll into a ball (conglobation), their diet of decomposing matter and their own feces (coprophagy), their lack of urination and drinking through a rear tube, their marsupium brood pouch, molting and shedding their two-piece shell, their ability to accumulate heavy metals like zinc, lead and copper, and their value as garden composters. They close with a plea to leave them alone and not treat them as garden pests. Includes some heavy metal band banter and an ad read for iHeartRadio.
topics: invasive species spread via plant trade

segments.title: Opening and regional names
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode about pill bugs and debate what the bugs are called in different regions, with roly polies being the Southern term.

segments.title: Range and origin
segments.summary: The hosts discuss where roly polies are found in the US and that they originated in the Mediterranean, spreading worldwide through the international plant trade.
topics: invasive species spread via plant trade

segments.title: Crustaceans and land adaptation
segments.summary: Roly polies are identified as crustaceans related to crabs, lobsters and shrimp, not insects. They are the only crustacean fully adapted to land and breathe through gills; the hosts note twelve US species. Their ball-rolling response is discussed.

segments.title: Conglobation and waste
segments.summary: The term conglobation is introduced for rolling into a ball. The hosts say they do not urinate, excrete waste through their shells, and eat their own feces, which gives them another chance at nutrients.

segments.title: Drinking and brood pouch
segments.summary: The hosts describe drinking through a tube-shaped structure at the rear, and females carrying eggs in a marsupium for two to three months, with young sometimes returning to the pouch.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Hosts joke about the number of facts and take a break.

segments.title: Molting and shell pieces
segments.summary: Roly polies are arthropods that molt. Their shells come in two pieces, and they can drop the back half, so a bug missing its back shell is normal.

segments.title: Harmless and composting
segments.summary: The hosts say roly polies don't sting, bite or carry disease, and that they act as composters because of their detritivorous diet of decaying plants and dead animals.

segments.title: Heavy metal bands tangent
segments.summary: A banter tangent in which the hosts name heavy metal bands, including Crocus, Sabbath, Dio, Iron Maiden, White Lion and Testament.

segments.title: Heavy metal accumulation and garden damage
segments.summary: Roly polies can accumulate heavy metals such as zinc, lead and copper in their bodies, which may let them live in polluted areas. The hosts say they may drink moisture from plants but do not eat through garden vegetables.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give a reminder to leave roly polies alone and close the episode, followed by an iHeartRadio credit.
